messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: metering-write-lag (P1) — service: metering-ingest-aggregator. Symptoms: write queue depth rising, consumer lag > 30m. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-1402

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification: incident INC-1402 created and paged to oncall (Eli).

Eli (oncall-sre): ACK. I'll take primary. Checking offsets and the consumer group.

LogsBot: Recent error sample from aggregator: 
```
ERROR ingest_consumer - Failed to write batch to ledger: timeout after 30s (error=WriteTimeout)
WARN kafka.client - Fetch failed for partition 34: offset 1254321 (lag=640k)
```

Maya (eng-ml): seeing a steady increase in unprocessed events in the staging S3 buffer too. Looks like backpressure from the write path.

Eli (oncall-sre): hypothesis: DB connection pool exhaustion + slow writes causing raft of backpressure -> Kafka lag -> PD fire. Will check DB connection metrics and container OOMs. Running: `kubectl top pods -n prod | grep metering-aggregator`

Sam R. (platform): I can spin up an extra aggregator replica and increase connection pool as a short-term mitigation. Suggest `kubectl scale deploy metering-aggregator --replicas=6 -n prod` and bump `DB_MAX_CONN` via configmap.

Anna (billing): what customers might be impacted? If ingestion stalls for >1 hour we risk undercounting tokens for today's invoices. We need an invoice hold flag available.

Tess (finance): pls confirm scope ASAP. We can place a manual hold for invoices created in the last 24h for affected accounts.

Eli (oncall-sre): scaling now. `kubectl scale deploy metering-aggregator --replicas=6 -n prod` -> pods creating. Also restarting the aggregator pods to clear potential leaked DB connections: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/metering-aggregator -n prod`

LogsBot: New pod logs show DB writes recovering but slow: `avg_write_ms=850` (baseline ~50ms).

Maya (eng-ml): I kicked off a quick health check job to compare current ledger counts vs expected based on API events. SQL I ran: 
```
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(tokens),0) as tokens_ingested FROM ledger.events WHERE event_time > now() - interval '2 hours';
```
Current result indicates ~11.8M tokens ingested vs expected ~13.5M — ~1.7M tokens behind (~12.6% delta).

Anna (billing): that delta is material. Please hold invoices for customers with >500k tokens until we confirm reconciliation. I'll prepare a list.

Sam R. (platform): I'm enabling a fallback mode: flip `METERING_WRITE_TO_S3=true` so aggregator will persist raw batches to S3 for durable storage while DB recovers. Applying configmap patch now.

Eli (oncall-sre): DB pool metrics: `active_connections` near max, replica read replica healthy, primary CPU at 98% during spike. I asked DB infra to add a few extra writer capacity slices (in progress).

DB Infra (via LogsBot): DB horizontal shard autoscaler triggered but waiting for maintenance window. ETA 45m for safe scale.

Maya (eng-ml): Meanwhile starting a backfill pipeline that will read from S3 fallback and re-ingest once DB healthy. Starting job: `python tools/backfill_from_s3.py --prefix=metering/tmp/2205554321/ --dry-run=false`

Eli (oncall-sre): After scaling and restarts, consumer lag decreasing. Running `kafka-consumer-groups --describe` shows lag dropping from 640k -> 120k in 8m.

Tess (finance): thanks. Anna, can you share the list of customers to hold? We need names + invoice IDs.

Anna (billing): posted list to finance drive and flagged in the billing dashboard. Also created manual hold for high-risk invoices: HOLD-#2205.

Maya (eng-ml): backfill job progress: 35% processed, estimated time to finish re-ingest ~ 50m given current throughput.

Eli (oncall-sre): mitigation status update: primary mitigations applied: extra replicas, rollout restart, fallback to S3 enabled, backfill job running. Consumer lag now < 20k. Marking incident as being actively mitigated.

pagerduty: PagerDuty update: Incident INC-1402 acknowledged by Eli at 2026-03-14T15:03:21Z. Auto-escalation suspended.

Sam R. (platform): note — I pushed a temporary config change to DB pool: `DB_MAX_CONN=500` and `DB_CONN_TIMEOUT=10s`. Will monitor for connection errors.

Anna (billing): estimate for token shortfall after backfill completes: current delta ~1.7M, backfill should cover >95%, final expected delta <80k tokens. I'll coordinate reconciliation and make sure invoice math uses final ledger state.

Eli (oncall-sre): backfill finished. Re-ingest success: 1.66M events reprocessed, ledger delta closed to ~18k tokens. Running final consistency check: 
```
SELECT expected_tokens, actual_tokens, (expected_tokens-actual_tokens) as delta
FROM metering_counters_summary WHERE window='last_24h';
```
Result: delta per account under threshold for all accounts on hold.

Anna (billing): thanks — releasing manual holds. Will run billing job and double-check.

Tess (finance): go ahead; mark invoices as safe.

Eli (oncall-sre): moving incident to resolved. Will create follow-up postmortem — suspected root causes: DB writer saturation under traffic spike + insufficient circuit breaker on write path causing cascading retries. Action items: implement write-side circuit breaker, add DB autoscale preflight, improve alerting thresholds to detect database write latency earlier.

pagerduty: Incident INC-1402 resolved by Eli at 2026-03-14T15:15:50Z.

Maya (eng-ml): +1 to postmortem. I'll attach backfill job logs and the SQL queries used for reconciliation.

Eli (oncall-sre): filing incident doc: https://confluence.example/incidents/INC-1402-metering-writebackpressure. Assigning postmortem owners: Eli, Maya, Sam R., Anna.

Anna (billing): tagging support to notify any customers who asked about invoice timing: #support will post a templated update.

Sam R. (platform): proactive improvement: I'll add a dashboard tile for `avg_write_ms` with a 5m alert to page earlier.

Eli (oncall-sre): thanks team. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
